name: goldener-research
description: Local skills and plugins for the goldener-research repo.

plugins.name: sync-idea-issues
plugins.description: Sync GitHub issues labeled "idea" into the matching topic IDEAS.md file, then branch, commit, push, open a PR, and close the source issues.

plugins.name: sync-researcher-issues
plugins.description: Research GitHub issues labeled "researcher" (or researchers named directly, e.g. "add NAME to goldener research"), find relevant papers, recursively check each paper's co-authors, requiring 3+ relevant papers (the shared one included) for new researchers and recursing up to 2 levels deep, then branch, commit, push, open a PR adding everyone found to the matching topic RESEARCHERS.md file(s) (with BIBLIOGRAPHY.md entries), and close any source issues.

plugins.name: sync-paper-issues
plugins.description: Research GitHub issues labeled "paper" (or papers named directly by title/link), confirm relevance, recursively check each paper's co-authors, requiring 3+ relevant papers (the shared one included) for new researchers and recursing up to 2 levels deep (adding them as researchers when they qualify), then branch, commit, push, open a PR adding every paper found to the matching topic BIBLIOGRAPHY.md file(s) and every qualifying researcher to the matching topic RESEARCHERS.md file(s), and close any source issues.

plugins.name: sync-lab-issues
plugins.description: Research GitHub issues labeled "lab" (or labs named/linked directly), resolve the lab's website and publication list, confirm which papers are relevant, and track authors reaching 3+ relevant papers as researchers (checking an author's own broader record when the lab's output alone falls short, and recursing into co-authors up to 2 levels deep), then branch, commit, push, open a PR adding papers to BIBLIOGRAPHY.md and qualifying researchers to RESEARCHERS.md, and close any source issues.

plugins.name: sync-conference-issues
plugins.description: Research GitHub issues labeled "conference" (or conferences named/linked directly, with an optional year), resolve the requested edition (proposing the closest edition(s) or stopping when the given year has no published program, or using the latest one when no year is given), fetch its accepted-paper program across every format (orals, posters, keynotes, and co-located workshops, deduplicating a paper accepted under more than one), confirm which papers are relevant, and track authors reaching 3+ relevant papers as researchers (checking an author's own broader record when this edition's output alone falls short, and recursing into co-authors up to 2 levels deep), then branch, commit, push, open a PR adding papers to BIBLIOGRAPHY.md and qualifying researchers to RESEARCHERS.md, and close any source issues.

plugins.name: sync-theme-issues
plugins.description: Research GitHub issues labeled "theme" (or ML themes named directly, e.g. AutoML or curriculum learning), run a bibliography search ranked by citation count and keep at most 20 of the most cited papers confirmed relevant to Goldener, recursively check each paper's co-authors, requiring 3+ relevant papers (the shared one included) for new researchers and recursing up to 2 levels deep, then branch, commit, push, open a PR adding papers to BIBLIOGRAPHY.md and qualifying researchers to RESEARCHERS.md, and close any source issues.

plugins.name: paper-review
plugins.description: Review one paper given by its title (or picked at random from the bibliography when none is named, optionally within a theme): look it up in the goldener-research bibliography (bundled script searches every BIBLIOGRAPHY.md) or online when it is not there, read its full text and save a short self-contained HTML review: title, authors, link, innovation in 1-2 sentences, the paper's main figure, then why it is data-centric AI, main innovations, and limitations.

plugins.name: short-paper-review
plugins.description: Write a smaller summary of one paper review: the paper with its link, its main innovative idea, and its role as a data-centric building block within the AI lifecycle, formatted for a publishing target (plain text by default, LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Mastodon, newsletter, Slack, ...) with its social-media elements (hashtags, mentions, length limits, threads), always marked as AI generated, and adapted to the context given (angle, audience, length, language, the user's own take, Goldener mention, external text and links). Written from a paper-review review, an existing one or one created by calling the paper-review skill (kept or temporary), and saved as a text file, never published.

plugins.name: propose-goldener-features
plugins.description: Propose the top 3 next features for Goldener: read Goldener's main branch and its existing issues, read every idea (IDEAS.md) and paper (BIBLIOGRAPHY.md) of this repo, rank grounded candidate features and write an implementation plan for the best 3, then present them one by one and ask the user whether to create an issue for each in goldener-data/goldener.
